narr: A stationary boundary lingered near the Ohio River through the day. The boundary provided a lifting mechanism for a moist and unstable air mass over eastern Kentucky. Torrential rainfall on top of already saturated soils caused streams to rapidly rise and flash flood at several locations.
ev: Flash flood waters peeled up pavement on Climax Rd between 4 and 5 miles outside of Mount Vernon.
Flash flood waters were reportedly flowing over Quail Rd.
Flash flood waters reportedly observed carrying trees across Old Waynesburg Road near the 500 block.

Swiftly flowing water from the Left Fork of Caney Creek was flowing across KY-611 making it impassable. A video on social media showed traffic backed up on either side of the flooded roadway unable to cross and waiting for the water to recede.
Pictures showed several inches of water flowing over East Main Street in Mount Vernon.
Norton School Branch Road closed due to flowing water over the road.
Road closures reported on Buckeye and Hummel roads due to flash flooding.
Video showed an estimated at least 1 foot of water flowing over Goochtown Rd.
Pictures show flash flood waters surrounding mobile homes along Freedom School Rd.
A car was reportedly stranded at the intersection of Little Robinson Creek and Robinson Creek roads.
Kentucky State Police reported a car stranded by flash flood waters at the intersection of KY-610 and Indian Creek Road.
